A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
integrons use a replicative mechanism for both strand exchange and resolution.

the attC + attI site-specific recombination reaction is a two-step process: first, a single strand exchange on the bottom attC site strand; second, replicative resolution of the resulting Holliday junction.
the attC site is replicated after the first strand exchange and then reannealed to its attI partner to form a double-stranded HJ, which is resolved by replication of one of the attC strands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resolution of a single-stranded recombination intermediate does not follow the classical pathway of two consecutive strand exchange reactions.
the replicative resolution pathway is not limited to recombination between dsDNA substrates.
replicative resolution of a HJ formed during the insertion of a gene cassette in an integron can be achieved without any strand exchange other than the one that forms the HJ.
